bl:add-ms-21593-c.name: Tupaia
bl:add-ms-21593-c.role: Navigator from Ra‘iātea and contributor to the chart project
bl:add-ms-21593-c.detail: Eckstein and Schwarz place Tupaia at the centre of collaborative drafting with members of the Endeavour crew in 1769–70. They propose reading routes from different points of departure.

bl:add-ms-21593-c.name: James Cook
bl:add-ms-21593-c.role: Endeavour captain named in the shelfmark’s catalogue entry
bl:add-ms-21593-c.detail: The British Library files this sheet under his name with the date 1769. This establishes the catalogue’s attribution. Te Ara identifies the same shelfmark with Tupaia.

nka:holm-collection-fig390-a.name: Kunit of Umivik
nka:holm-collection-fig390-a.role: Inuit map maker from Umivik named in the Walters label
nka:holm-collection-fig390-a.detail: The label credits Kunit with the carved coast piece and names the Greenland National Museum and Archives as lender.

nka:holm-collection-fig390-a.name: Gustav Holm
nka:holm-collection-fig390-a.role: Expedition leader who received and described the carvings
nka:holm-collection-fig390-a.detail: Holm published the exchange and distinguished the mainland coast from the separate island piece. He reports Kunit carving and explaining the chart, including where a kayak could be carried between two fjords.

nka:holm-collection-fig390-a.name: Hans Harmsen
nka:holm-collection-fig390-a.role: Greenland National Museum curator and archaeologist
nka:holm-collection-fig390-a.detail: In a modern account of the pieces, Harmsen emphasizes how their shapes helped one person tell another about a route and its coast.

usnm:e432083-0.name: Marshallese chart maker, name unrecorded
usnm:e432083-0.role: Maker whose work the Smithsonian classifies as a preparation aid
usnm:e432083-0.detail: The exact object record attributes the chart to Marshallese knowledge. The collection window of 1940–1959 describes when it was collected and leaves its making date open.

usnm:e432083-0.name: R. Naomi Cannon
usnm:e432083-0.role: Donor and witness to a repair
usnm:e432083-0.detail: The Smithsonian records Cannon’s account of using string to hold broken sticks together. Her account concerns the condition of this accession.

aph:founding-docs-item-104-i.name: Dhuwa artists of Yirrkala
aph:founding-docs-item-104-i.role: Artists of this petition’s painted surround in the parliamentary caption
aph:founding-docs-item-104-i.detail: The Parliamentary Education Office attributes the 14 August entry to Dhuwa artists and describes the designs as expressions of Yolŋu law.

aph:founding-docs-item-104-i.name: Jock Nelson
aph:founding-docs-item-104-i.role: Member who presented the Dhuwa petition
aph:founding-docs-item-104-i.detail: The National Archives identifies Nelson as the presenter in the House of Representatives on 14 August 1963.

aph:founding-docs-item-104-ii.name: Yirritja artists of Yirrkala
aph:founding-docs-item-104-ii.role: Artists of this petition’s painted surround in the parliamentary caption
aph:founding-docs-item-104-ii.detail: The Parliamentary Education Office names Yirritja artists separately for the petition dated 28 August 1963.

aph:founding-docs-item-104-ii.name: Arthur Calwell
aph:founding-docs-item-104-ii.role: Member who presented the Yirritja petition
aph:founding-docs-item-104-ii.detail: The National Archives identifies Calwell as the presenter in the House of Representatives on 28 August 1963. The typed display paper and the signed original have a separate copy history.
